note: Newest first. MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: MINOR for new features, PATCH for fixes. The top entry is the app's version.

items: "Set when you take each one" is now the same folded panel on Today, Quick and Lite. To remove a supplement or change everything about it, the panel links to More, then Supplements & routine.
Lite: "Add a supplement or powder" can mark it Only as needed, with a most-per-day limit.

New Lite tab: big buttons for I'm up, Eating now, Done eating for today and Going to bed. Each supplement can be set for a moment (on waking, with a meal, at bedtime), a time after it (30 min to 3 h), or 30 min or 1 h before a meal or bedtime, counted from your planned meal times.
Log what you ate from Lite, Today or Quick: pick a meal, or pantry foods with amounts (¼, ½ and up), set the time, and save it as one of your meals to pick next time. Edit or remove what you logged.
Ticks stay in step: supplements, meals and Kitchen closes ticked in one view show in the others.
Alerts while the app is open: a banner and chime when something comes due, plus a notification if you allow them. Settings are on Lite.
Start page: open the app on Quick or Lite (one or the other), set on those pages or in Phone settings.
iPhone time pickers now save when you tap Done instead of closing after the first turn.

Setup guide: the first page shows how long it takes (about 10 minutes). The Reminders step now also sets times for water, the evening treat, moving frozen meals to the fridge, and cook day, and explains the minutes-before alerts.

Setup guide: new "Your routine" step. Tick common steps like walking, breath work, dry brushing, a sinus rinse or a sauna, or add your own. Each one gets how often (every day, some days or every other day), at home or in town, and times a day. A clock time is optional.
Setup guide: medicines and supplements now ask how often, times a day, and "only as needed" with a most-per-day limit.
Setup guide also covers: diagnoses like fatty liver plus your own, an evening check-in, walks after meals, a water goal, your frost months for "local now" in the pantry, and opening the app on Quick.
My diagnoses lists every condition, including blood sugar, mold, celiac and HSV, as single lines you tap to open. Ticking one there turns its starter list on or off.
My diagnoses: add your own diagnosis with its name, foods to avoid or limit, and questions for your doctor.

New: My diagnoses, under More. Add or remove a diagnosis any time, not just in setup. Fatty liver (MASLD) is new: a draft food list (alcohol, sugary drinks, juice, added sugar, refined starches, fried and processed meat), each food can be turned off, plus questions for your doctor. Sources: NIDDK, AASLD 2023, EASL-EASD-EASO 2024.
Pantry: move an item you added to a different section with the menu next to it.

Pantry: "local now" follows the season where you live. Set your last spring and first fall frost months (or no frost), and change when each item counts as local. Sources: NOAA Climate.gov and Penn State Extension.
Warning boxes are now one line you can tap to open: the home-screen data warning and the spacing check.
Removed the Not confirmed yet box and its labels from supplements and the checklist. Taking it now is what turns a supplement on or off.

As needed supplements: tick As needed on a supplement and it leaves your checklist and reminders. Tap Took it on Today or Quick to log the time. You can set a most per day and get a warning when you reach it.
Supplements and routine: one Every day box instead of ticking each day. Untick it to pick days.
Supplements no longer ask Where. They go with you, so their reminders use the at-home lead times.
Phone: updates now show up the next time you open the app, instead of getting stuck on the old version.
Phone: new setting to always open the app on Quick, with its one-tap buttons. It's on the Quick tab and under Phone shortcuts. If you leave the app for 5 minutes or more, it goes back to Quick.
Every other day: pick the first day you take it, instead of it always starting the day you turned it on.
How many times a day: take something 2, 3 or 4 times a day without picking clock times. Leave Times blank and it shows up that many times on your list to tick off.
Setup guide: a tip on the food list and lab steps for getting the text out of a PDF or photo with an AI chat app, with a ready-made request to copy.
Setup guide: already have a list of foods you avoid? Pick a text file or paste it, check what the app found, and add it all at once. Lines like Avoid:, Limit: and OK: sort the foods under them.
Setup guide: the Lab results step can also read a text file of results.
Setup guide: a new Lab results step. Paste the text of a lab report and the app picks out each test, result, unit and range for you to check before saving.

New setup guide: a brand-new copy of the app opens with a few quick questions about what you're managing, foods you avoid, medicines, your day, who you cook for, your kitchen, your pantry and reminders. Every step can be skipped.
Run the setup guide again any time from More, or from Times & reminders. It shows what's already set, so you only change what you want.
Today shows a Finish setting up card if you leave the guide part way.
Allergy picks like milk or eggs now catch dishes made from them (cheese, omelets) in the checker and pantry, and leave things like coconut milk alone.
My rules has a What I'm managing line, which also goes on your visit summary.
Meals: 34 more starter recipes, with stand-ins (any one of chicken, tofu, beef or pork, for example), so more meals fit what you have.
Pantry: things you type in now count for the meals that use them. Salmon counts as fish, kale as cooking greens, brown rice as a grain.
Meals I can make now counts meals you can make without buying anything, including ones that need a batch cook first.
A spice or oil you haven't ticked no longer stops a meal from counting as ready. You can turn this off in the pantry.
Meals that don't fit your food rules move to their own group and stay out of Fill. If one stand-in breaks a rule, another is used.
Pantry: an edit button on items you added, to fix the name or fill in what a label photo missed.
With the computer app and a second window or phone open, a change no longer gets lost after it says Saved. Changes from both are kept.
With the computer app, a change typed just before closing the window or switching away is no longer lost.
Backups: new Combine with a backup file, to bring a phone and a computer copy together without losing either.
With the computer app, an old open window can no longer save over newer changes from another window or phone.
Clearer warning: on an iPhone, removing the home-screen icon erases its data, so save a backup first.
Labs: paste a whole lab report (or copy it from a photo or PDF with Live Text) and save many results at once.
Pantry: items you add go into the right section (or pick one), and any item can be removed from your list.
Grocery mode opens reliably from More and the bottom bar.
Fiber: set the ramp start date on My rules; with no ramp, Today shows your fiber goal.
Fix a meal: type a meal's ingredients and the meal checker suggests swaps, trims and adds that follow your lists and limits.
A gentle check-in when a supplement or routine step hasn't been ticked off in a while: keep it, change how often, or pause it.
Version number and this What's new list.
Bottom bar on every page, so a home-screen app can always get around.
Quick view and phone tap shortcuts.
Installed copies now pick up new versions.
Tap to add water (sizes you choose) and a simpler home page.
Evening check-in: how did I feel today?
Look back over 7 to 30 days, and a For my visit summary; both print and download.
Grocery mode for the store.
Automatic daily backups.
Food breaks: take a break from a food until a date, with a low-arginine list for cold sores and HSV, common food groups, or any food you type. Planned meals can be swapped and come back after.
Daily rhythm settings: wake and bed times, fasting window, walks after meals, food order, water goal by weight.
Sources page; every food rule shows where it comes from.
Daily checklist, pantry planner and meal checker that work offline. Starter food lists (drafts).
